utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I indicated that I feel that the 1700 one is accurate, and I believe that because a large body of other evidence supports that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you could look at those pages that I provided you, from page 4483 all the way to 4484, if you could find anywhere in those pages where we are talking about this particular incident and this particular witness, where it is that you have also informed the Honourable Members of your Trial Chamber, that there was another witness with a much different time frame, one that would reflect 9.00 or later -- the incident to have occurred. And where is your explanation as to why you discount that version versus the one that you liked -- that you have accepted, which is the earlier one. Is there anywhere in your testimony that you can see that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection to compound, especially when there's these sorts of suggestions in the question, if we could go point by point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll break it down, Your Honour, I'll break it down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: First of all, we'll see whether the Witness gets it or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe I can answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I peg the time at 1700.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But that's not my question, I want --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to explain this, sir. You will have to be patient.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Give me the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, no, Mr. Karnavas. Let the Witness finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Very well, very well. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I base it off the testimony of the first witness that was discussed. I didn't know and I still don't know at this point whether the testimony we just discussed is or is not before the Court. I just -- I can't that one. Is it my -- okay, I assume that it is. Again, I don't believe that it's my function as the analyst, and that's why I don't include this type of information in my report except to set context, that it's my role to try and determine before the Trial Chamber which witnesses are truthful or accurate in which particular issue. I believe that with this respect I hinge on the time of 1700, and I believe I've been able to forward a series of exhibits which corroborate that. If it's an omission on my part that I should have mentioned as part of this that another witness had indicated a later time - and to be quite honest, Mr. Karnavas, apparently it slipped my mind that as far as 9.00 is when he thinks the actual execution part in large scale takes place, then that is an omission on my part and I will apologise before the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Thank you for the admission, however you would agree with me that you do mention the one account. And so -- and I just want to tag you a little bit on that one, because you do seem, you do seem, when it's favourable to the Prosecution to be providing some of that information, maybe not in your report but certainly in your testimony. And so, I would say that your answer is rather inconsistent with what we have here, because your other statement was helpful, beneficial, in favour of the Defence, perhaps. Certainly it was not consistent with the Prosecution's theory, and that is that these -- this incident occurred at or around 5.00. And so would it be fair to say that a conclusion can be drawn that here is yet, here is yet, one more example where you are cherry picking, you are selectively stating that we have this information from this witness while at the same time failing or omitting, albeit in this instance, and I take your point, by accident, but failing and omitting other evidence that might be equally as valuable to this Honourable Trial Chamber in determining what exactly happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm going to object on the form of the question, and it completely misconstrues both the evidence that the witness -- the two Kravica warehouses -- if you look at this both Kravica warehouse witnesses say shooting started at roughly the same time. You may recall how big and long the Kravica warehouse is and how it's divided into two different chambers,. So this is a complete misconstruction of the facts, and we'll hear Dean Manning will describe the warehouse and some of the damage that was in the warehouse. But aside from being undecipherable, just look at that question, it's a misconstruction of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we came to the situation that the Defence counsel made a long statement which seems to me that is his conclusion. And also the Prosecution gives some explanations which might be to testify instead of the Witness. I'm not quite happy with this kind of practice. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think you have made your point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I was moving on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you have to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I was moving on. I was moving on before the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now with respect to -- just take a, maybe, a lighter note. You testified with respect to the documents that were sent by the Bratunac Brigade daily reports or others that occasionally if the commander or the designated person who was supposed to -- whose name was on the paper was supposed to sign it, that if he did not sign it, that you would find the word za there, which meant for so and so. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the practice, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And I take it -- and then you indicated that it would be poor -- it would be irresponsible, it certainly would not be correct, for someone to sign for the commander without having the "for" before it, because it might give the wrong impression that perhaps the commander himself had signed the document, should the reader of the document not be familiar with the commander's signature.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And just -- I just wanted to show you. There's several documents here, all Prosecution documents. If I could have the assistance of Madam Usher. Just I call these little vignettes, just to show you -- if you could go through the documents I'm handing you, and if you could read for the record the numbers of the documents at the bottom of the page. They all have P numbers.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. In this particular case it's P416.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is there za there for the commander?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. It's the commander's signature block, and this is Lieutenant Micic's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact for the typewritten version we don't have a za and in the handwritten version we don't have a za. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You generally won't find a typewritten version in the -- za in the typewritten one, but where you're supposed to see it is the handwritten one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. If we go to the next one, the next document --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: She didn't give me the whole stack.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I apologise. We can put them on the ELMO. We can go through those real quickly.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: 503 would be the next one, sir?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I assume you want me to go back and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I would like you to go through all of the handwritten versions, and if you could find one that says -- if you can find one that has za.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is 18 July, and it just has the name, no signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So that's 18 July. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is 419.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What date is that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This would be 11 July. And this is just a signature block, no signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this is P501, a signature block, no signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And P502, in what appears to be the same handwriting, a signature block and no signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So can we glean anything from this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, clearly in this particular respect, four of the documents I believe have no signature at all, and the fifth one has Lieutenant Micic's signature with no za.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So I take it that the rules are not always followed, it would appear?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular case they were sloppy with practice, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. That's all for the za's. I think we finished that chapter rather quickly. All right. Now, there's one other matter, another small vignette. And what I would like to do in this particular case, I would like to hand you some documents. And it would be -- okay. If I could hand you these two documents. One is -- we'll just identify them first. You will note that one document is from chapter 5 of your, this is the narrative I believe.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And we're going to be focusing on paragraph 5.4. If we could put that on the ELMO, and I don't know whether --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which one do you want on the ELMO --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This would be from page 40 of your narrative, and on top of the page it has an ERN number 01134334. And I wanted to -- if we could read it, read the portion of it, the first sentence for context. And then we'll discuss it. "The order also stated that the corps command had sent a message to the RS Ministry of Defence requesting that busses from state and private companies be mobilised and placed under brigade commands in whose area the buses were being sought." Do you recall writing that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In fact I believe you might have discussed it because there is an exhibit, is there not, Exhibit P427, from which you derive your information for this particular portion of your narrative?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I need to see that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have 427. No, that's -- I don't -- okay, I've got 427.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you look at the third paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah. Well, 5.4 is the one that we talked about.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I mean if we compare the two, and I'll read the last -- I'll read that paragraph from paragraph 4 to P427, so you can put that on the ELMO, if you wish, third paragraph. It states: "The corps command has sent a request to the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska demanding that the Ministry of Defence office in Sarajevo and Zvornik obtain by 12 July 1995 all the buses available from state and private owners for the use of the commands of the brigades in whose areas the buses are being sought. The areas concerned are: The municipality of Sokolac, Rogatica, Visegrad, Han Pijesak, Vlasinica, Milici, Bratunac, and Sekovici. They shall help the municipal offices of the Ministry of Defence to procure the buses rapidly and direct them to Bratunac." Okay. Now, if we look at that translation of this particular document, which is dated 12 July 1995, and we look at your paragraph that you attribute, we can conclude that you are accurately describing in your narrative what purports to be on this particular document, correct, on P427?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, here is -- I would like to show you now a document, a revised translation, a revised translation, of this particular document that was done today. And we have extra copies for everyone, but if you could put one on the ELMO and we could put -- we could distribute the others to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we identify, revised by who.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey may not ask that question. He should know by now that we have the official translators. This was done on an expedited basis, and I also want to thank on the record the Registry, because we had them do it twice today, twice. So we would like to commend the Registry for assisting us in this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we look at this paragraph and we will -- if I could read it now. It says here, this is the corrected version, and in fact I've also, for the record, discussed this with the translators in the booth to make sure that we had the correct translation. Now let's look at the revised translation, based on the original document. "The corps command has sent a request to the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska demanding that the Ministry of Defence office in Sarajevo and Zvornik obtain by 12 July 1995 all the buses available from the state and private owners and place them on disposal. The commands of the brigades in whose areas the buses are being sought: The municipality of Sokolac, Rogatica," and it goes on. Do you see the difference?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And also it would appear that -- it also indicates that they are -- if we go on: "That they shall help the municipal offices of the Ministry of Defence." Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact my certainty is not so good, but having discussed this matter with the gentlemen in the booth, it would appear even one word or two words are missing even from this corrected version, and that's the DK which can be found on the original version, which would mean Drina Corps. And if we were to look at the original in Srpski, and I have it -- do you have it available?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it. Is this what you're looking at?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You'll see right before the date 12.07.1995, right immediately before that, you see DK, do you not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And would that not reflect the Drina Corps, unless you don't know?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I mean, I've seen it as DK. I've seen it as KDK. So I mean it may well mean that, I just don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, having looked at this corrected translation, which of course you are not to blame at all --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apparently that will be the first thing in the last six days I'm not responsible for.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, now. Mr. Butler, would you not agree with me that perhaps with respect to this one paragraph in your narrative, we might need to revise it slightly?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Clearly I would revise it on the basis of this revision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And so -- and the revision would take place in a way that it would reflect that it's -- they're under the Drina Corps with the brigades assisting and not that these buses from state and private companies are placing them under the brigade commands. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe that -- yeah, in this respect it would be to the Drina Corps and not down to the brigade commands. I mean, that's the change in the language, yeah, that's fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I thought so. Okay. Now, we took care of that vignette. That will be the last vignette for today. Now, I just wanted to end with discussing a little bit about the MUP. That will be our last topic more or less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think the new translation should have a number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We are going to get a number today, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please inform the Court Deputy about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I didn't want to make the list grow any longer, but it appears that it's growing on its own, Your Honour. It would be D86/1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we could -- okay. Now, if we could switch to MUP a little bit. It's my understanding from hearing your testimony that your interpretation of one of a particular order that was issued by Mr. Kovac on 10 July 1995, which has been marked for identification purposes as P157 - and I will give it to you shortly but I'm sure you know what I'm talking about. This is the one that places the MUP under the -- or resubordinates MUP under the Drina Corps. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically it resubordinates the second Sekovici and the 1st Company of the PJP to the Drina Corps. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, now --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all MUP in general, but those formations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. If we could look at it just a little bit, and then we're going to go backwards. It's the last paragraph --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Paragraph 5. It says that: "On arrival at the destination, the unit commander shall contact General Krstic of the corps chief of staff." Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, he must. He doesn't have an option. He has to contact him. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is how I read this, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now -- and it's my understanding from listening to you that you interpret "shall contact" as shall be resubordinated to the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. When we discussed this issue specifically with Lieutenant Colonel Borovcanin and asked him specifically what that meant, that is what he told us. He says that he took this to be him contacting General Krstic and putting himself under Drina Corps -- or General Krstic's direction. So that's where we derived that from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At this point, Your Honours, I would ask that we strike that answer from the record, only in the sense that Mr. Borovcanin is on the lam. In other words, he is not to be found. We don't have access to him. There is a statement, but again We cannot confront him with respect to whatever he might have said to the Office of the Prosecution. So in light of that, there is no other basis from -- in light of that, I would ask that that portion, that answer, be struck or at least, at the very minimum, that the Trial Chamber recognises that we are at a distinct disadvantage in not being able to confront the gentleman. And therefore, this answer should be given no weight at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey. Any response to this request?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. As I think we've discussed, I have asked Mr. Butler to try to refrain from answering hearsay from major figures that we don't have available to cross-examine if his answer did not involve that. And I think he has tried hard over the several days to do that. And his questions regarding some hearsay, even though an expert under the common law can refer to hearsay, for the reasons Mr. Karnavas stated, we have tried to have Mr. Butler avoid going into statements like Mr. Borovcanin. And I can only assume Mr. Butler felt an answer -- to properly answer the question, he needed to reference Mr. Borovcanin. And of course Mr. Butler wants to tell you the complete truth regarding my instructions, he's taking them into account. So I would leave that with you and Mr. Karnavas and Mr. Butler to sort it out. Again, part of that instruction to Mr. Butler is based on my common law experience because Mr. Borovcanin is not available and is a potentially vital character in this. So it makes it difficult to use his information before you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it is a rare practice for the Trial Chamber to strike something off the transcript, but we have heard both parties on this issue. And later on when we elaborate this piece of the evidence we will take the submission of both parties into consideration. You may move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I know you can't strike it, but I have to at least go into it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So we have here contact, but we don't have anything that would give us some comfort, at least in this -- from this particular paper that would give specific instructions to Mr. Borovcanin as to what exactly his tasks will be once he contacts General Krstic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this paper it does not specify anything beyond what his task would be. No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And if we look at the preceding paragraphs, we can see what Mr. Borovcanin was tasked, at least with respect to the mobilisation and to where he was supposed to go to and at which time he was supposed to report and to whom. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to the mobilisation, which units would be pulled, and where he was to deploy, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I don't want to go into great detail on the rules and the law, though just a fair warning, I'm fully prepared to. But I believe you've already testified to the effect that when the special police that are under the Ministry of the Interior are to be resubordinated to the VRS, in other words, attached to them, that there would need to be, one, authorisation from the President or the Ministry, or his designated representative. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And we also touched a little bit upon this, that to ensure that the MUP would not be mistreated or placed unnecessarily, perhaps, in harm's way by the military, that along with that order, one, the VRS, the army itself, would first have to specify in detail the exact nature of their request for having the assistance of or for needing the assistance of the MUP. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The limits are that the army has to specify the tasks and that the MUP can only be employed within the confines of those tasks. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if I understand it correctly, not only does the army have to specify the tasks, but also the Ministry of the Interior in its own order, the order that would resubordinate the MUP to the army, would also specify in great detail the tasks that would be given to MUP. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that would normally be the case, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And it would appear, it would appear, that somewhere along the line there must have been some sort of a dispute between the army and the Ministry of the Interior, because there was a document that was generated by none other than the highest authorities with respect to the usage of MUP and resubordination. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are a number of them. If you can get me in the neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll get you in the neighbourhood. I thought I was -- I just wanted to tease you a little bit. The document is from Dr. Karadzic. He issued an order. It's -- it looks like it has a D number, D62. Do you see that? I think we go on to paragraph --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I'm familiar with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You're familiar with this. And this is dated April 22, 1995. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it seems to have been signed -- it would have the original, a copy of the original, it has the official stamp and a signature that I would suspect is that of Dr. Karadzic, the supreme commander.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that it is or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. But his name is there and the stamp is there. And I take it you do not have any particular reservations as to whether this order was in effect or came into effect. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I believe this order or the general guidance is in effect, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, we already have a law that clearly outlines what we've been discussing, that is, when MUP can be used, under what circumstances, and how their tasks are to be defined. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But here it would appear that irrespective or regardless of the law, the supreme commander felt compelled to issue a specific order, grounded in the law that was already in existence and expected by the various parties to comply with. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. There was as a -- because of -- or what this reflects is a result of confusion or, more accurately, disagreement between the army and the MUP as to what that meant on any given occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So on paragraph 1 it states: "The Main Staff of the Army shall henceforth define more precisely and concretely their request for engagement and employment of MUP units in combat, in accordance with provisions of Article 14 of the Law on Application of the Law on Interior Affairs during imminent threat of war and state of war, item 4 of the order," and it describes the Official Gazette which happens to be a special edition number 1. So from here it would appear that the President, the commander in chief, is saying to the Main Staff that they must define concisely and concretely their requests for engagement and employment of MUP units. Now, question: Do we have anything that would give us an indication of what exactly the Main Staff had asked of the MUP, that would be precisely and concretely?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to just Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one document that I have is the document from the morning of 12 July from Vasic where he describes the contents of -- or he describes in some detail, the 0800 meeting on 12 July, and he notes that the army and the MUP have received their tasks from General Mladic. I don't know that that particular report goes into specific detail exactly with what those tasks are. It may and it's just slipping my memory, but that is the one -- the first report with respect to the MUP that I have in that nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But here we have a document that was generated on 10 July, and obviously if Mr. Borovcanin is to report to the commander of the Drina Corps --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The chief of staff, I apologise. The chief of staff. At that time it was still chief of staff, one would expect, would they not, that there would be some sort of request in writing by the Main Staff that's spelled out with specificity, precision, and concretely their request, and also a document that would correspond to that. In other words, an order to the MUP, so as to when there was this contact between Borovcanin and Krstic they could -- they would at least be on the same wavelength. Would you not expect that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We don't have it.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We don't have it, and to my understanding the army did not request that this unit be withdrawn and brought into the Srebrenica area. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's probably why we don't have it and why there is some ambiguity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So if they were not requested, if they were not requested, by the Main Staff, as one would expect, then I take it they came into the area uninvited?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not -- uninvited by the army, I would probably agree. But certainly they were directed there by superior authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And if they came without any specific order and if we are to believe the laws in this particular order were in application and were being followed, one cannot then, one cannot then, conclude, as you have, at least based on the face of the particular document from Mr. Kovac, that on the 10th when Borovcanin is asked to contact, to contact, the chief of staff of the Drina Corps, that that in and of itself meant that those MUP units were being resubordinated to the Drina Corps. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In isolation, this one order does not do that. Again, a lot of it for me is the context of what occurs afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, it's time for a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Butler, we were talking about MUP before we took our break. Now, as I understand it, the rules provide, the law provides as well as this order, that when there is a resubordination, the logistics support for the police unit are to be provided by the other unit, that is, the unit of the VRS. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The unit in which zone they're going is responsible for providing support.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to show you then something that might help us out a little bit. It's P458 for identification purposes. If we were to look -- do you recognise this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And it would appear that this document is a request made by Mr. Vasic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. There is his report up to his MUP leadership.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And does he not state -- and this report is to his superiors, right, within the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The Republika Srpska, the office of the Minister, the Bijeljina public security department, and the police forces headquarters, which is the police staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And from reading it, at least from the top of the page, it's unclear whether it's a report, whether it's a request, or maybe a combination of both. But if we were to go to the paragraph that is numbered number 1, he does seem to indicate, does he not, that he urgently needs 10 tonnes of petrol. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that would be on July 13, 1995. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And would petrol not be part of the logistics support that would be expected of the army to provide to a resubordinated unit from the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Petrol would, but I think the 10 tonnes part is the indicator that this is -- the requirements are well outstripping the unit's abilities to provide them. We are talking about, my understanding, the 10 tonnes of petrol needed to move the civilian population. So I think that's different than the organic requirements of the unit itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I think there is very little disagreement that the MUP was involved of the evacuation of the civilians on 12th and 13th in Potocari. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, their presence is noted on 12th and 13th, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you indicated to us earlier that a request had not been made by the VRS for them to appear there, correct? Or at least you're unaware of that they were requested by the VRS to be there and to be resubordinated to them. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. That is correct. There's nothing that indicates that the VRS had asked for their presence prior to their arrival.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And of course, and of course, here it is that they're asking for 10 tonnes of petrol to their Ministry of the Interior. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And there's no indication in this particular report or request that the reasons that they urgently need the 10 tonnes of petrol is because the army to whom -- or the army unit to whom they are resubordinated are unable or unwilling to meet the logistics support, as they are required under Article 14 of the law promulgating the implementation of the law on internal affairs during an imminent threat of war or state of war in the order from Dr. Karadzic of 22 April 1995. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm confused by the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the answer is that in paragraph 1 they're specifying that they need the fuel to finish the evacuation. I hope that was the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And it appears, does it not -- well, what I'm saying is that in this request, though they're saying this is what they needed for, they're not stating here that the reason they need the fuel is because the VRS, or in more particular terms, the Drina Corps, is unable to meet its obligations under Article 14, that is, to provide the logistics support to the MUP unit that's resubordinated to the VRS, as prescribed by the law and by Dr. Karadzic's order.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, it doesn't specify why they can't get the fuel from the local institutions in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And from this, therefore, we cannot conclude from this particular document, we cannot conclude or it will not assist us in determining whether indeed the MUP has been resubordinated to the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In isolation, the document doesn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Doesn't say that.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And certainly the issue of fuel isn't an indicator of that one way or the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But even if we were to look at Mr. Kovac's order that's dated the 10th of July, where he requests Mr. Borovcanin to contact or he orders Mr. Borovcanin to contact the chief of staff, General Krstic, and we look at this particular request, together they both don't provide us any additional assistance in getting us to where we might wish to go, and that is in determining whether the MUP were indeed resubordinated to the VRS pursuant to the order of 10 July 1995 issued by Mr. Kovac. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree, sir. Linking these two together won't get you to that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, there was one minor point I wanted to point out. It has nothing to do -- this is the second time in one day that I will point out something that may be of some contention and which is of no -- you are not a participant of. And that is in the translation. Now let me show you what has been -- the other exhibit. It has been marked as -- it has a 65 ter number; it's 51. It's -- and it's D64/1, D64. So now if you could just briefly look at it and you will see at the top, one says: Draft translation, that's D64. And then of course we have Prosecutor's P458. And if we could focus on the very first sentence. It would appear, would it not, sir, that in the very first sentence it states that, and I'll just read it: "During the meeting held this morning with General Mladic, we were informed that the VRS, Army of Republika Srpska, is resuming with the operation towards Zepa and is yielding," and I'm underscoring that word, "yielding all other tasks to MUP," and then it lists the tasks. Now, if we go to the translation, the translation is slightly different. Rather than say "yielding," it says: "Leaving all other tasks to MUP." I was wondering whether you caught that distinction.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The version that I used in the narrative I believe is cited by -- is the draft translation. We didn't have final translations when I had to have the narrative published.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't catch that as a difference, and I'm not sure that yielding or leaving may be just a term of semantics. I don't know that there's a whole lot of significance behind it. I await your view on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, when you see the word "yielding," what is your interpretation to that, just so we can have a -- I want to make sure that my interpretation is similar to yours.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this respect, I look at it as -- that the army is giving all the tasks to the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, are they giving or are they allowing?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I believe it's directive in nature. I mean, if that is the bone of contention, I believe this is directive in nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, from this, just from this, if we were to use yielding or leaving it all up to either one, this doesn't get us any closer either to our earlier question, our earlier dilemma?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would disagree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Insomuch as, and again the key piece that's still missing in this context is the one from Vasic on 12 July, which notes that the army and the MUP are taking their orders from General Mladic. And again, this is -- if you insert that and you continue on through time and events, again the fact that now here on the 13th at some time in the morning, they're now being informed that the army is resuming their operations towards Zepa and is directing -- again, yielding, in my sense, is directing in nature. A variety of these tasks with respect to moving the civilian population out of Potocari and also dealing with the Muslim column, I think it does play in context.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. So in other words, because of that you seem to be implying or inferring that indeed they were resubordinated, because it has the word "yielding" in it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, is it possible that you can have the VRS and the MUP operating in the same zone of responsibility whereby they are cooperating with each other, they are coordinating with each other, yet one is not subordinate to the other?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The problem that you have is that, again, coordinating and cooperating is something that's directed by the superior command. Somewhere there has to be some level of superior command which will dictate that. Now, taking that model and the practical application, on the ground I believe that you have the elements of the army along that road or adjacent to each other, which would be Bratunac, the MUP, the 5th Engineers, the 65 Protection Regiment, they're coordinating their activities. The next step up would be the superior command which would do that. Would it be the Drina Corps or would it be the Main Staff? And I believe that given the wide range of activities, I believe that it's the Drina Corps. So that's why I say -- that's why I have problems in abstract, because somewhere along the line between cooperation and coordination, there has to be a command relationship involved which would dictate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Are you familiar with Mr. Obrenovic's statement in which he gave to the Prosecution after he had negotiated his plea agreement, where this issue of subordination, resubordination, came up?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm generally familiar with it. I don't know the specifics. Again, I have to remind you, during the period I was moving my family back to the States, so there might be gaps in my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Fair enough. Let me show you then, it might help you a little bit. We've discussed this already with Colonel Obrenovic. Let me show you page 110, 110, of the transcript of Mr. Obrenovic's statement. It was, I believe, introduced as -- the entire statement I believe was initially introduced as D52/1. And this is a statement of 4 June 2003. And we have a question. I'm going to go to line 10 and it's a question PM, that would be for Peter McCloskey. "Okay. The MUP were under the command of the army at this time. Is that right?" And the answer is: "On the 19th, I don't think that it was, unintelligible. We were conducting the sweeps separately. After the corridor was closed, each group was conducting its sweeps separately. Already on the 18th and further, unintelligible. On the 22nd, there was a joint operation between the asphalt road and the gravel road in which combined units participated. "Q. It's hard for me to imagine the MUP working in the same woods that you are working in, without being under the control of the army. That would be very dangerous situation for both of you. "A. You are correct, but it was separate." Now, are you familiar with this line of questioning and the answers to which Colonel Obrenovic gave after, after, he had already pled guilty to one of the counts in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I'm familiar with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And it would appear, would it not, that in his answers here that we have a situation where MUP and a unit of the VRS are working in the same general vicinity, and it would appear that they must be coordinating and cooperating in order to -- in order for both units execute their own tasks, while at the same time not posing a danger to the other and not one being resubordinate to the other. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. In this respect, I believe that is what he's trying to describe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And in fact he even went further and described the same thing when he testified under oath to the general -- to the same line of questioning. Is that correct, or are you unaware of that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think -- I may have seen it somewhere after the fact, but I'm not aware of that. I take your word that he probably said the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And the record would reflect that. Now, let me -- so here we have at least one instance where we see that you have MUP and a unit of the Drina Corps working side-by-side, and yet one is not resubordinated or subordinated to the other. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular instance I believe you have the Zvornik Brigade and you have the MUP operating in adjacent areas, and they are not subordinate to one or the other; that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So in light of your answer when we get back to the document that's dated 13 July 1995, one by Mr. Vasic, when we look at that and we look at the first sentence, the one that is not numbered, where we seem to have this interpretation difference, whether it's yielding or leaving it all, it would appear, would it not, that we could easily conclude as well that at this point in time, MUP is coordinating and cooperating with the VRS, yet not being resubordinated to them. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that I would do that, because we do have the 17 July order from both the VRS, which designates a zone that their forces are going to operate in. We do have a 17 July order from Kovac which designates a zone, and then we have the Zvornik Brigade doing their operation. I don't have those same specific separation orders on the 13th. So that's why I'm reluctant to conclude that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But also what we do have -- we also have missing in this particular case with respect to the 10th, the 11th, the 12th, the 13th, we don't have, one, anything that is precisely and concretely -- a request that is precisely and concretely to the MUP with respect to assistance from them?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And we also don't have --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the 10th --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: For the 10th, right. And also likewise we do not have anything that precisely specifies the responsibility of the units -- of the MUP units that are going to be resubordinated to the VRS, the corresponding one. We don't have that either?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. We don't have -- and we do not have the internal discussions of those meetings, other than what is on paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Yet, pursuant to the order by Dr. Karadzic, which is grounded on Article 14 of the law itself, we can both, we can both conclude, or we can both agree that those -- that request and that order, that is, the requests of the MUP which would be -- which would precisely and concretely specify their needs and the order from the MUP that would precisely and concretely outline MUP's responsibilities, those things are required by law. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's compound. I think he meant requests from the army also.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Request by the army and also the order by MUP to its own units of exactly what their responsibilities would be, those are mandated by law. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Both those are directed under the law. I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And those are missing in this case?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether they are missing or whether they were never published, I don't know. But we don't have them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Or they were never issued.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. With that, Mr. President, Your Honours, I have no further cross. I do have one technical issue that has been brought to my attention that I believe last week, it must have been last Friday, I noted for the record that the rules of services of security organs in the armed forces was D84, when in fact it is D85. So I want to make that correction, and other than that I have nothing further, Your Honours. And I appreciate your indulgence in giving me the additional time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Butler.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Karnavas. Any cross-examination, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, I believe that we will stick to the time limits that you have set for us, and we planned to use this afternoon and then also Wednesday, just as you said. We have changed and amended some of our questions. And we are prepared at this point to begin, but perhaps it would be good to perhaps have a five-minute break, because I provided Mr. Butler with the list of all the exhibits which I will be asking him about and also these are exhibits provided by Mr. Butler in the two binders of his. So I think it would be more effective and faster if we can just arrange the questions chronologically and in order and that will help us to save time for our cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes, we'll break for ten minutes and we'll resume at ten minutes past 1.00, I guess. --- Break taken at 12.58 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Are you ready, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Now we are ready to begin, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Butler.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Since I come from the continental system, I will first of all stick to what is written in the indictment which is the reason we are here, and secondly, I will try to put more direct questions as necessary in order that we can achieve or attain the truth. I would like to look at Exhibit P398; it is a document which is the personal card of Dragan Jokic. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Every superior officer in the Zvornik archive had such a card reflecting his status and position in the Army of Republika Srpska and the rights and duties arising from that. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We found a large number of these. For the most part they were for the officers serving in the brigade command, yes, sir. I'm not sure if it was everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you perhaps tell us, if you know, which service in the Zvornik Brigade worked on these personal files, the cards, where were they found?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If memory serves, these were found in the office of the assistant chief of staff for personnel- and mobilisation-related issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would I be wrong if I said that that person in question is named Mihajlo Galic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be correct for July of 1995. I could not tell you if that was still correct at the time we seized these records.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like just to focus on column 12, the date of joining the Army of Republika Srpska. In your testimony you stated that this is 16th of May, 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. It should be 16 May 1992. I hope I didn't misstate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you're right, the 16th of May, 1992. Could you please look at Exhibit D39 first and then we can comment on it. Could the usher please hand the document to the Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for the record I would just like to say that this is a document which we received from our investigator on the ground. Page 2 is the translation of the original document, the translation into English. The origin of the document is the command of the 359th Engineering Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, can we agree that this is a record on the effectuated [as interpreted] transfer of duty dated the 19th of June, 1992. It was carried out in the barracks at Ladjevci and the transfer of duty was effected of -- for the position of assistant commander for morale between Lackovic Dragoslav duty assuming officer and Captain First Class Dragan Jokic, the duty relinquishing officer?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I believe you said 19 and it reflects 16, but yes, sir I agree with what the document is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is the 16th of June 1992. According to this document it appears that Captain Dragan Jokic came off duty and relinquished his duties in the Army of Yugoslavia on the 16th of June, 1992. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He -- in this particular instance he relinquished the position for assistant commander for morale and guidance. The unit is the 359 Engineering Battalion. So he did officially relinquish it on this date, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we conclude, based on this, he then took up his duty in the Zvornik Brigade on the 16th of June, 1992, and that it can also happen that perhaps the numbers were switched when this information was entered into his personal card?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to item 12 or line 12 of his personal card, it is not uncommon that the date 16 May 1992 is used as the date joining the VRS, because it is my understanding that that is the day that it turns out that they used to designate the official standing up or creation of the Army of Republika Srpska. So in that respect, this date is fairly common among many personnel records. He may have arrived shortly after; he may have arrived before. So I'm not sure -- I don't tag the date 16th May, as an indicator of exactly when he may have arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That is precisely what we wanted to say. Would you agree with me that it's possible that this was also on the 16th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. It is a possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I just also want to ask, since I'm again basing this on what is stated in the indictment, could you please repeat to us exactly when the Zvornik Brigade was established.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information that I have indicates that the Zvornik Light Infantry Brigade, as a component of the VRS, was established on 1 June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So if it states in the indictment that Dragan Jokic was a member of the Zvornik Brigade from the moment that brigade was formed, and it was formed as you say on the 1st of June and there is the possibility that he actually joined it on the 16th of June, so can we agree that this was after -- he came to Zvornik after the Zvornik Brigade was formed?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mean, certainly based on this document, and I again forgot the exhibit number, it indicates that he officially left his duty at the 359 Engineering Battalion command on 16 June. He may well not have arrived until 16 June 1992, or sometime, a day or two or five, after. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go a bit further. On the 5th of November, 1992, a meeting was held at the Drina Corps command in Vlasenica. And this meeting was devoted to the operations or actions in Srebrenica. I know that you did not focus in your report on the period of 1992, but still I would like to ask you if in the documents which were seized from the Drina Corps you had the opportunity to have access to the minutes of this meeting of the 5th of November, 1992, where Dragan Jokic refused as the chief of staff of the Zvornik Brigade to take part in this attack, with the explanation that it was his task to defend Zvornik and not to attack Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps if I can clarify. The records that we have do not include the Drina Corps records for this period. We were unable to locate them in the course of the investigation, therefore we did not search the Drina Corps headquarters. So I think because we don't have those records, I have no way to confirm or deny that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I assumed that, but it was my duty to put the question to you. The next question is: Would you be surprised if in the course of the proceedings we offered evidence that this fact was actually one of the reasons why shortly after this meeting Dragan Jokic was replaced from his duty as the chief of staff of the Zvornik Brigade. Would this possibly be the reason for his being replaced?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may well be. It wouldn't surprise me insomuch as shock, but if there's evidence that supports that, I mean, it may be a fair conclusion, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now move to Exhibit P372. These are the instructions for the work of the commands and the staffs; is that so?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I know that on Friday you responded to Mr. Karnavas's questions on this document already, so that is why I reduced the number of my questions on this exhibit. But I would just like to briefly go through this document with you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what is implied under the term "management" or "control" in the instructions for the operation of the staffs and headquarters.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that it's implied. I believe it is implicit in these regulations, that control is a function of management or control -- it may be that management is how one exercises control. I believe, again going back to 13, 14, and 15, I prefer to use their definitions rather than my own. Now, with respect to the phrase "management," and that is generally used with respect to a supervisory function, although it can be used with respect to a command designation. It is most often used with a supervisory function.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So let's not try to analyse what the supervisory function in the control aspect means; this is item 3 in the instructions. And it states there that: "Control in the armed forces is characterised by two forms. Control, as a social relationship, and control as a process of work of the superior officers and the staff commands and other bodies." Am I right when I say that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so. I'll pull the exact page up; it's not on the exhibit. So if I can get right to that. This is paragraph 3 that you've just discussed, sir? Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's move to paragraph 4. It states -- it says that: "Three kinds of relationships are essentially manifested in the control system of the armed forces: Command relationship, functional relationship, and staff relationship." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So from this definition of the term "control," can we conclude that the term "control" is broader than the term "command"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I know that we have an additional problem, and that is interpreting. In the indictment, control and command were defined with one and the same term, direction. For the record let's just make it clear. Let's repeat that control is a broader term than the command, and it contains the command structure, the command activity, as well.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The phrase "control" is a broader one, and the command portion of that is one of the components. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The other two terms contained in the control are the function and the staff.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Kindly, Mr. Butler, let's -- let me draw your attention to item 10, where it says that: "The control and the command as a process of work is a process based on the principle of joint staff work in which the most important thing is that every task has to be planned, organised, and set by a command document, and it has to be coordinated and controlled."

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The way I understand this provision, and you correct me if I'm wrong, control implies the realisation through command, amongst other things. Am I right in thinking that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Control is how the task is realised, and command is part of that. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I would like to direct your attention to item 13 of this instruction on the work of command staffs, which says: "Command is a process function of control and command acts communicate command decisions and activate the process of task execution, and it is reflected in commands, orders, directives, and instructions." So we are talking about five forms of command as documents. Am I right in thinking that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it says it's the four forms and in 13 it's: Command, orders, directive, and instructions. Decisions -- or the act to communicate, they communicate the command's decisions, so I think we're at 4, not 5. Am I misreading this?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that you're right, because in the original text there are orders and instructions, so these are the two documents issued by the commander to issue -- to exercise command and then follow other things that you've just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now let me draw your attention to item 19 of the instruction which says as follows: "The system of command and control in the armed forces has three levels."

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The three levels are as follows: Strategic, operational, and tactical. Am I right, sir?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Who is in charge of the strategic level of control?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can put up the last part of that paragraph that wasn't on this list, maybe it will help us in that respect. If we transmit this to the Republika Srpska VRS, it would be the supreme command or in this case the supreme commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And who is in charge of the operational level of control and command?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this level, it would be the combination of the Main Staff and the corps command, I believe, would make up the operational level.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we also talk about the republican stance of the Territorial Defence, at least up to the point when units of the Republika Srpska were formed?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we're referring to the early 1992 period, yes, sir, the -- not necessary -- the republic ones would be the strategic level, and the provincial TO staffs would be the operational level -- or not provincial, probably regional would be the better word that I've seen it translated as, regional TO staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I agree, the state was not organised as a federation with provinces. I'd rather call these regions or even lower levels of the organisation of the Territorial Defence. And finally, the lowest level, the tactical level of command and control, who is it who deals with that level?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, within the context of the military units, it would be -- there was, in fact, one division still in the VRS, but for the most part we're talking about brigade level and below. And if you were going to the TO staff level, that would be at the municipality level. And then below that, many of the larger villages or areas had their own subordinate TO units or TO staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me see if I understood you correctly. So at the lowest levels, the tactical level of command is discharged by brigades as tactical units?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And in that sense, the way I understand this concept of control, this is a process involving several participants and institutions. Am I correct in thinking that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, depending on which point in time we're discussing, by 1995 the process of control with respect to the military is generally much clearer with respect to the supreme command through the Main Staff and the military chain of command. If we're referring to the period of May -- or April/May 1992, it is much more fragmented and you will have a much greater degree of control by the various regional and municipal TO staffs at the time, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But in any case, in 1995 when the structure of the Army of Republika Srpska was well-defined, the control implied a chain of several participants involved in that activity. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think by 1995, the chain is well-defined. You have -- and again as we've defined, you'll have the command relationship, you'll have the functional relationship, and you'll have the staff relationship. I do not believe what you'll find is outside non-military entities which would be exercising control through this chain.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely so. And if we take such a concept of control and if we take these three levels of control, the strategic, the operational, and tactical, can we define and say that one staff officer can be in charge of control?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on the level, I don't know that one staff officer could be in charge of control, but one staff officer through a functional relationship could exercise within the competencies control over subordinate staff in that respect. So I don't know that it's broadly -- one staff officer could be in charge of control, but again going down the functional relationships, a senior staff officer could exert some control, again limited within that -- the competencies of that particular staff officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The way I understand it, direction or control, with these three levels your answer is no, a staff officer cannot do that. Am I right in thinking that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure we're on the same issue. If we're talking about for a staff officer at the strategic level, could he exercise control all of the way down to the tactical level, he can do it indirectly through a functional relationship, yes, sir, again limited to within the competencies within that particular staff officer's assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm trying to understand you. Let's one again define one thing. A staff officer cannot be involved in the strategic control, in the operational control, or in the tactical control. He only can assume a part of the functional side of the control within the scope of his authorities as a staff officer. Am I right in thinking that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely so. What I'm trying to do is take us back to the indictment and our objections to the indictment. Direction, the term direction, the term control, according to the instructions on the work of staff commands is a broader term than the function that a staff officer has. Am I right in thinking that, in saying that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The term "control" is broader than the specific function of a staff officer. That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this may be a good opportunity for a break. I'll be moving on after the break, and I will take the witness through various counts in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I hope we could come into something more specific after the break. And we'll resume at 3.00 in the same courtroom. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.45 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, before we start, I think there's a scheduling announcement. First, on Wednesday afternoon we'll sit in Courtroom II, starting from 2.15 until 7.00. We'll try to finish the testimony of this witness on that afternoon. And because of other obligations, I myself won't be able to attend the first sitting and possibly the second, but definitely I will be here during the third sitting, if there is. Another announcement is that we'll cancel the sitting in this case on Thursday and Friday, since today we sit extra time. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic. Please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would kindly ask before we proceed to try and remove a misunderstanding that was pointed to me when we checked the transcript. All my questions when I mentioned the word "control," I wanted to say direction. That is the term which is used in the indictment. All of these questions in the transcript are interpreted as "control." I understand that this is not just a grammatical difference. In my language, the meaning of the word control is just a segment of the word direction, one segment of direction. Your Honour, in the indictment -- in seven counts of the indictment, my client is charged with direction and not with control. So in that sense, I would kindly ask for a correction. All my questions were about direction; a term found in the indictment. From Mr. Butler I received an answer that an officer, a duty officer, cannot be engaged in direction in the way it is defined in the instruction on the work of command staff. So that would be all in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, your correction is in the transcript already.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to move on. I would like to explain why I have asked all of these questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, good afternoon once again. May we please proceed?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, in your analysis what information have you reached, who was involved in the burials in Orahovac on the 14th and the 15th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The assets that were involved in the burial operation in Orahovac were personnel and equipment from the engineering company of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 15th in the morning hours, were there any other assets which were used in the burials, I particularly refer to the communal company, and this was testified here by a witness. So did you find anything else in your analysis? Were there any other assets or institutions involved?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that some of the equipment came from Birac Holding, which was one of the state-owned companies, and there were other pieces of equipment - perhaps not directly subordinate to the engineer company, but belonging to the greater logistics branch of the Zvornik Brigade, although I think the trucks in question did come from the engineer company or those that were assigned to the engineer company.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that on the 15th of July in the morning, a unit of the public utility company or, better say, employees of the public utility company from Zvornik also participated in the burial operations?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know if it was a unit per se. I believe that there were perhaps one or two individuals that were associated with the public utility company.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you learn about the assets which were involved in the burial operations in Branjevo?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Please, can you tell us which institutions were involved in the burial operations in Branjevo on the 17th.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, there would be elements of the engineering company of the Zvornik Brigade.
