And up until about 1400 hours, after that, he went to the frontline where there was fighting and he stayed there until about 2000 hours on the 14th of July. At that time, at 2000 hours on the 14th of July, he returned again to the command of the Zvornik Brigade and stayed there until the morning, until about 7.00 or 8.00 in the morning. Then he returned to the frontline, Parlog, Snagovo, Krizevici, we'll mention other places later, and then returned at about 10.00 to the Zvornik Brigade command. That is what we want to prove, we want to establish before the Trial Chamber. Although, we know that there is no reason to say that Jokic was in a position of command, we have cleared this matter up. But we want to establish the truth, we want to demonstrate what the truth is. And this is why I want to go through all the exhibits that deal with what we are discussing and the Trial Chamber will determine whether this is correct or not. I would like to go through all these exhibits with you systematically, could you help me to do this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, sir, I'm at your disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Butler. I assure you that we'll try to deal with this very rapidly and to prove all of this. Could you please have a look at Exhibit D57, it's the book of the notes of the duty officer in the brigade. It's Exhibit 507, 5-0-7, 507.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone for Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I will also show you our exhibit, D53. Could the usher please show it to the witness, because it's at the beginning of the book that was provided by Obrenovic and I would like to have some comments on this, too. It's marked D53. Can we do this, Mr. Butler? When you carried out your analysis, did you conclude that at a given moment in time, in July 1995, that the 9th Battalion was in the Zvornik Brigade, too?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with a designation of a 9th Infantry Battalion. I'm wondering if what we're talking about in the Nisici [Realtime transcript read in error "Nedzici"] Battalion, if that wasn't the battalion that was assembled by the Zvornik Brigade and became part of the 4th Drinski Brigade which then went to Trnovo. But organisationally speaking, I'm not aware of a 9th Battalion, per se.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. At this point I'm going to be objecting to the impeachment of Dragan Obrenovic on this issue, whereas Dragan Obrenovic was not presented with this material when he had a chance to be questioned. It's improper to impeach a witness through another witness when you have not given the witness in question a chance to respond. Now we're in the situation where we, you can see, have to bring people back. It's just -- now, that is something of the common law, and I understand Mr. Stojanovic is new and didn't do the cross-examination of Mr. Obrenovic, but this does put the -- a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. In this respect I agree with you, Mr. McCloskey. Mr. Stojanovic, I'm a little bit puzzled by your kind of opening statement of seeking the truth of this matter. I think in your cross-examination the question you asked should be closely related with the testimony of this witness in the direct examination or with the interest of your client. I know there is a dispute about whether Mr. Obrenovic was at the brigade headquarters on the 14th or not. I think this is a point, and you mentioned it before on another occasion is about the meeting in the corridor or at the end of the stairs, that occasion. I think this is a point which is closely relevant to that issue. But if you are going to ask all the questions concerning of the deployment of the army of the Zvornik Brigade at that time, that subject is too big. I don't think they are quite relevant to the case we are faced with.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood, Your Honour, and I accept it. But I just wanted to say one sentence. I am using the exhibit that was delivered to the OTP by Obrenovic and then this document was forwarded to us by the OTP. That was the book that was in Obrenovic's possession until the moment he pleaded guilty. And secondly, I'm trying to use this expert to corroborate a thesis that Mr. Butler analysed, and that is the presence of the members of the inner circle of command of the Zvornik Brigade on the 14th in the headquarters. And thirdly, I am trying to say that the part that he had mentioned now, and that is the meeting on the 15th between Obrenovic and Jokic is not true. So if I depart from any of these thesis that were given to me to prove, I'm going to withdraw my questions. But I'm not intending to cross-examine Obrenovic through Mr. Butler. I would never do that. And if at any point you think that I'm doing that, I'll withdraw my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have an objection to Mr. Stojanovic getting into this topic of who was present at the various command posts. My concern was particular instances that he's referring to that may deal specifically with Obrenovic presence should have been questioned by -- should have been put forward to Mr. Obrenovic. Now, at this stage I will not object to it. In fact, I've asked counsel before if they do have any information on this subject, the Prosecution would of course like to see it. But I'm just saying that as a point of practice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic, let's come directly to your second and third point you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will speed up then.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, we are talking about the unit that you have mentioned, we can call it the 9th Infantry Battalion or the Drina Battalion, in any case it was the unit that was transferred to Nisici. Do you know who the commander of that unit was?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name escapes me, but that is something I can get my hands on very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If I put it to you, Mr. Butler, that this could be somebody called Milenko Kajtaz, would that refresh your recollection and agree with me?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This unit was lined up in the morning hours of the 14th and the person that I've just mentioned reported and then they went to Nisici to carry out there task in the presence of Obrenovic. I am going to try and prove it in the later course of this trial. I just wanted you to confirm that this unit did indeed go to Nisici on the 14th, in the morning hours of the 14th?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would dispute your date. My understanding, if we are talking about the same unit, is that this particular unit was sent down to the Sarajevo battlefront back in late June of 1995. And maybe, like I said, I'm thinking Nisici and I keep seeing on the screen Nisici. And I know they're two different places, so -- there may be some confusion. We're not talking about the same unit. The unit that I'm referring to deployed to the Sarajevo battlefront in late June of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I agree with you. You are talking about the departure for Trnovo in June 1995. But we are talking about the unit which was sent to Nisici on the 14th. This is an area between Sarajevo and Kladanj and Olovo. But this is not the unit you're referring to. If you're not in a position to confirm this, I completely understand. In any case, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that respect, I am not familiar with the deployment that you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's look at the logbook of the duty operations officer that you have in front of you. We are talking about the 14th of July, the 2nd or the 3rd remark entered by Jokic.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I ask you to direct me to a page number, sir, that might just make it a little faster.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't give you the page number in the English version, but let me help you. This is making a note of the units that need to be employed, in other words, how many troops came from which battalion. This battalion, the 3rd Battalion, the 4th Battalion, the 2nd Battalion, and the 5th Battalion, this is the third order which was issued on the 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me. For clarification, is counsel now agreeing that this book is valid and that Jokic did, in fact, make these writings, because inferred in his question that would be correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think you are too eager to confirm that. Could I hear from Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Obviously I'm not going to say anything about that today, however the further course of this trial will show clearly what Dragan Jokic did write, what he didn't write. We will certainly get the answer to this question and the answer is not even going to be disputable at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I object to playing games, offering this -- we're guessing whether this is valid. Inferred in his question was that it was valid. Let's just get down to -- what is your position? We shouldn't have to guess and play games.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe Mr. Stojanovic is not in the position to answer this question. But you may continue your question and you may answer it tomorrow or you may not. Anyway, the Bench will arrive at a conclusion at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour. It is up to the Chamber to decide on the quality of this exhibit. We have already stated our position about this exhibit and we will continue stating our position on every entry in this log. However, the Prosecutor has already used this exhibit, Mr. Butler has already commented upon this document on the chief, and I believe it is my right to ask questions about this document without actually stating my position on the quality of authenticity and validity of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour. I just -- the form of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may move on, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Is this the passage that you're referring to, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And I just wanted to ask you to give us your comments. It says: Transport pursuant to Obrenovic's approval. Can you comment on this, sir? Immediately after that, if you can help me, at one page later there is a digression in which it says: The Prime Minister talks to the duty operation officer and asks him when will Avala arrive in the base. Can you tell us whose secret code was Avala on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the preceding page or the next page?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Five pages later, five pages later.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's do page 8 first, if you don't mind, sir. I don't know what this means. It does, in fact, look like there are arrangements being made for a rotation of soldiers or the deployment of a number of soldiers. It says, again: "Transport pursuant to Obrenovic's approval", and that's all I know about it. I don't know whether they're going in a -- where they're going or whether or not they, in fact, even went. It's not evident from this at all. And my understanding of the broader situation within the Zvornik Brigade is that -- just like, for example, in the Bratunac Brigade, while they were planning for unit rotations, I don't believe that they actually sent them during this period because of the military situation. So this may reflect part of the planning process. That's probably about all I can tell you was my understanding on this. I don't really know all of what it means.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you agree with me that this implies, if it is correct, that this order can only be carried out on Obrenovic's approval. So Obrenovic is there and he is in command, because his order is executive and gives the green light to this -- these soldiers to start moving?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again the order can only be given out on Obrenovic's approval, that's correct. So Obrenovic is there -- I don't know his physical location. Certainly he's in the zone of the Zvornik Brigade. He is in command on the 14th, so I don't know that his physical presence is or is not required in order to make this happen. So like I said, I can agree with two of your positions, that Obrenovic is in command and he's making this happen. I just don't know the data as reflected on this page would lead me to conclude his physical presence or not. I just don't think we can make that conclusion, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Butler. I think it's on page 13 or 14 of the English version of this book and there is an entry: The Prime Minister then Mamba asked when Avala was going to come to the base and asked you whether you knew who had that pseudonym Avala at the time on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding is Premijer is the code name for the radio reconnaissance element of the Zvornik Brigade, not the Prime Minister. My understanding is that is what Premijer means in that context. I don't know who Avala is. So I can't be of assistance in that one. I have not heard that name before. I don't know where to associate it with.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If I said that Obrenovic confirmed that Avala was his pseudonym, would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This would be the first time that I'm hearing it. I must have missed it in the testimony. I would see no reason why you would misrepresent that, so okay, that's fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If that were correct, could I draw the conclusion that the radio relay device which was called Premijer, and which monitored Avala, was it via this means that he was asked when he was coming to the base, and on this basis can we conclude that the arrival of the person called Avala was expected in the command of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it's expected, but -- and again, maybe it's an issue of translation, but the reading that I get off of the English language translation is that they're asking when he's coming to base. I don't know that there's a response or any indication as to when he'll return or if he'll return. Again, maybe -- I leave open the fact that maybe the translation is not giving me a clear indication, but I can't make that conclusion from the English language translation that I'm reading, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the following page, could you just comment in response to the Prosecution question. Jokic, the heart of the delegation from Pilica. Are you aware of the fact that in the 1st Battalion, or the Pilica Battalion there was a man called Dusan Jokic and he was the commander of a mortar platoon in July 1995? His name was Dusan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir I'm not aware of that fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the surname Jokic is one that one comes across very often that you have come across it in a number of situations?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, sir, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll discuss this in greater detail. On the following page, there is a note that says: Report for the corps. You have also discussed this subject in the course of the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It starts with the words: "Tonight around 2020 in the wider area of Maricici," et cetera and you also mentioned when it was sent from the Zvornik Brigade to the Drina Corps. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I believe that is indicated in the interim combat report for 14 July.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I assume that you read the statement of Dragan Obrenovic in which he said how this interim combat report was sent to the corps command. Just to refresh your memory, I will say the following. He says that he was in position and this telegram is one that he dictated to his communications officer who sent it to the Zvornik Brigade command. They copied it out and then took it to the teleprinter room and sent it on to the Drina Corps. Do you remember that part of his testimony?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that's accurate, sir. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I assume that you also remember that in the course of his cross-examination he said that it was possible that this text hadn't been intercepted, even though before and afterwards JNA operatives intercepted conversations that they had, but this telegram wasn't intercepted. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had or had not, that by -- and I'm assuming by intercepted, we're talking about the Bosnian Muslim tactical intercept operators. Is that what we're talking about, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We're talking about the fact that the Bosnian operatives, BH army operatives didn't intercept this conversation, wasn't recorded by them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. So my knowledge that this particular intercept was not recorded or intercepted by the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So could we draw the conclusion that is possible, and later we'll talk about other pieces of evidence. Could we conclude that at that time Dragan Obrenovic was in command of the Zvornik Brigade and dictated the text of the interim report to the duty officer. Would you say that this was a possibility?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a possibility. I would just, however, have to add that even in the body of this particular document where we see this particular text, we don't see extensive blocks of reporting that later show up in a daily combat report. There is another document which Obrenovic did provide which does reflect what is going to be or what later becomes the text of the daily or the interim combat reports. But like I said, I don't know that -- while it's a possibility, I don't know how much weight I would put on it as something definitive. It looks to be a one-off example of that, and I don't know that I could draw a very hard conclusion on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Butler. With these two exhibits, we'll now try to get you to corroborate what we have been claiming. Could the usher just help us now. The exhibit marked D44, which is the statement given by Nenad Simic, could it be shown to Mr. Butler so that we can comment on it. Mr. Butler, could you just have a look at page 15, line 13 in Nenad Simic's statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd just like to draw the Trial Chamber's attention to the fact that this statement was given on the 19th of September, 2001, to the Prosecution after Dragan Jokic was taken to the Detention Unit in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And Mr. Butler, the Prosecutor asked him about the circumstances under which he was in the brigade on the 14th and 15th. And he said within the context of whether Obrenovic was present in the brigade, the witness answered: "Well, for example, a colleague of mine whom I know, he came to the office and ordered him -- gave him a task in the evening, at 8.00 in the evening. It was perhaps on the 12th or on the 13th. This administrator who hadn't come and on the 17th of July, Obrenovic was supposed to come. This was about the 14th after midnight, something like that. I know that he," and he is referring to Obrenovic, "would come to his office and he would leave his office. He would make phone calls, who knows what he did. He must have been speaking to someone." The Prosecution asked him: "Just a minute, before you go on. When did Obrenovic assign a task to your officer, Bojanovic [phoen]?" And the witness replied: "After midnight on the 14th." The Prosecutor then asked him: "What did it say? What did it tell him to do?" And the witness replied: "There was a point, there was an area in Zvornik, Zvornik was literally empty and civilians were engaged." This testimony clearly shows that a response to the Prosecution's question, the witness said: Around midnight on the 14th, Obrenovic was there. So with regard to your questions about the interim report, I would like to show the statement marked 45 through 3 if the usher could help me, please. It is Ljubo Bojanovic's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm going to object to the use of these statements. It's not asking Mr. Butler any question or refreshing his recollection or impeaching him. It's just used as additional evidence that Mr. Obrenovic was there on the 14th. We have 92 bis, we have a whole foundation of material that is designed to deal with these issues. So again, I would object to the form of the question of these statements coming in like this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I think there's some problems in the using of those documents. Well, Mr. Stojanovic, it's time for the break. Maybe you could think this issue over tomorrow and try to have your materials well organised. I hope you have to put a question to this witness. I understand that some issues here are relevant to your case, but the issue is that you have to put a question to this witness. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. So we'll resume on Wednesday afternoon, 2.15, in Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
